title: The Palindrome Machine
description: This small decoder transformer was trained from generated examples to classify symbol strings. Its task is simple to state; the computation it learned is not supplied. Characterize what it gets right and wrong, inspect its internal computation, and build a causal hypothesis that survives held-out tests.
behavior: Given a sequence over A–H, predict whether it reads the same forward and backward. The trained checkpoint receives beginning and final markers internally; classification is read at the final position.
task_goal: Build an evidence-backed investigation: establish the model's behavior, inspect attention and residual activations, propose a mechanism, then use targeted interventions to test it. Matching a component label or plotting attention alone is not a complete solution.
metric: Binary classification accuracy on generated palindrome and near-palindrome sequences
example_note: Try changing one mirrored symbol while holding sequence length fixed. Evaluation reports the final-position class prediction.
learning_objectives: Characterize generalization and failure cases across lengths and mismatch positions
Inspect cached attention, Q/K/V, head outputs, and residual activations with Python
Distinguish attention correlation from causal contribution using ablation or patching
Test whether a proposed mechanism generalizes to hidden generated sequences
hints: First measure accuracy by sequence length and compare palindromes with near-misses.
Inspect more than the final prediction: cache activations and compare attention across mirrored positions.
Take a positive sequence and change exactly one symbol at its mirrored partner. Predict which internal quantities should change.
Ablate or patch a candidate activation. Check whether the intervention changes the class margin in the predicted direction.
Compare your proposed intervention with a different head and vary mismatch position on held-out inputs.

explanation.canonical_solution: The checkpoint was trained with both random negatives and hard negatives that differ at a single mirrored pair. On the fixed validation sample it reaches 98.9%; it is about 98% on the mission's generated hidden set at lengths 3–12 and remains near 98–100% for most single-mismatch offsets. A single-head ablation sweep shows distributed early contributions: in one hidden sample, ablating L0H0 lowers accuracy by about 36.5 points and L0H1 by about 29.2 points, while ablating both together lowers accuracy by about 43.8 points, illustrating interaction and partial redundancy. For clean-to-corrupted patching, replacing the final EOS residual after layer 2 restores the class margin across the generated hidden near-misses; earlier residual patches recover less consistently. This identifies a downstream representation where the decision is available, but it does not explain how mirrored equality is computed. A stronger account should sweep patching over layer and position, analyze QK/OV and MLP/residual paths, stratify by mismatch offset, and compare against control positions.
explanation.caution: The model reaches only about 50% on lengths 13–16, which are outside training. Ablation and patching results depend on the generated input distribution. Patching the final residual is localization at the readout and does not establish the computation that produced that representation. No numeric grader can certify a unique prose explanation.
